item.title: Reciprocal mirror map derivatives, euler-twisted Gromov-Witten invariants, and instanton counts via quantum Serre duality
item.author: Irit Huq-Kuruvilla, Michael T. Schultz
item.description:
Irit Huq-Kuruvilla, Michael T. Schultz

Matched: Gromov-Witten · math.AG, hep-th · cross

We study mirror map derivatives as a means of relating the genus zero Gromov-Witten theories of an anticanonical Calabi-Yau hypersurface in a smooth, almost minimal Fano variety and the local Calabi-Yau formed from the total space of the Fano's canonical bundle with the euler-twisted theory of the ambient Fano. A precise relationship between reciprocal mirror map derivatives is obtained from the non-equivariant limit of quantum Serre duality for the euler-twisted theory of the ambient Fano as formulated by Iritani, Mann, & Mignon. This allows us to express the generating series of 3-point euler-twisted invariants as the derivative of the local mirror map with respect to the closed one. In low dimensions, this series is shown to be a modular form of Eisenstein type which has arisen before in this area. We prove integrality of the twisted invariants from this identification. The regularized small quantum $D$-module of the Fano is reducible, and we show it is equivalent to an inhomogeneous Picard-Fuchs equation governed by this generating series. The reciprocal mirror map derivative is then shown to be a generating function of local 3-point invariants, which recovers some known results for local Calabi-Yau threefolds and proves a conjecture of the second named author and A. Malmendier in previous work on local fourfolds. Explicit calculations for $\mathbb{P}^2,\mathbb{P}^3$ and $\mathbb{P}^4$ illustrate these relationships, which includes the vanishing of positive-degree ordinary genus-zero invariants for anticanonical elliptic curves and K3 surfaces, the recovery of the quintic threefold's instanton numbers, and finally some formulas for genus-zero invariants of local projective spaces.

item.title: Gromov-Witten Nonvanishing and Symplectic Deformations of Toric Varieties
item.author: Nathan Tausik
item.description:
Nathan Tausik

Matched: Gromov-Witten · math.AG · new

Let $A$ be nonzero in the cohomology ring of a smooth projective toric variety $X$. In this note, we observe the existence of a nonzero Gromov-Witten invariant of the form $\langle A, A, \ldots\rangle_{0, n,\beta}^X$ as a consequence of Iritani's work on the big quantum cohomology ring of $X$. This implies Koll\'ar's conjecture on the symplectic deformation invariance of rational connectedness in the case where $X$ is toric. If $X$ is moreover Fano and $B$ is also nonzero in the cohomology ring, we prove the existence of a nonzero Gromov-Witten invariant of the form $\langle A,B,*\rangle_{0,3,\beta}^X$ using Batyrev's presentation of the small quantum cohomology ring of $X$. We conclude with a few consequences of this nonvanishing result.

item.title: Hamiltonian GKM spaces via Gromov-Witten theory
item.author: Daniel Holmes
item.description:
Daniel Holmes

Matched: Gromov-Witten · math.SG, math.AG · new

We use equivariant Gromov-Witten theory to prove the generalised symplectic Mukai inequality for Hamiltonian GKM spaces with large pseudoindex or a special vertex, including smooth Schubert varieties. We also classify all Hamiltonian GKM graphs when the pseudoindex is at least the complex dimension, obtaining a Hamiltonian GKM analogue of the classical Kobayashi-Ochiai classification of complex projective space and complex quadrics. Of independent interest are our connectivity theorem for a low-magnitude subgraph of the GKM graph (reminiscent of Campana and Koll\'ar-Miyaoka-Mori's rational chain connectedness of Fano manifolds), and a local Mukai-type theorem that applies at each vertex. We obtain corollaries on reflexive Delzant polytopes that are purely combinatorial in nature.

item.title: Multi-quadratic equations associated with KdV-type equations
item.author: M. P. Kolesnikov
item.description:
M. P. Kolesnikov

Matched: KdV · nlin.SI · new

The potential KdV equation admits dpKdV as a full discretization. Similarly, most KdV-type equations admit multi-quadratic quad equations as algebraic condition on B\"acklund transformation. These quad equations also yield three-point discrete symmetries and ensure the commutativity of two symmetries corresponding to different lattice directions. In each case, the quad equation is either an ABS equation or a multi-quadratic equation of the Atkinson--Nieszporski class. For KdV, mKdV, potential Gardner and exponential Calogero--Degasperis, these are the equations $H2^*$, $A1^*$, $Q1^*$ and $A2^*$, respectively, and for the elliptic Calogero--Degasperis equation it is the primary model $Q4^*$.

item.title: Integrals of motion for the deformed $W$-algebra $W_{q,t}(D_l)$
item.author: Michio Jimbo, Takeo Kojima
item.description:
Michio Jimbo, Takeo Kojima

Matched: KdV · math.QA, hep-th, math-ph, math.MP, nlin.SI, quant-ph · cross

The deformed $W$-algebra $W_{q,t}(D_l)$ of type $D_l$ possesses an infinite family of commuting elements that can be viewed as a two-parameter deformation of the classical Hamiltonians for the KdV hierarchy of type $D_l$; these conserved charges are termed local integrals of motion (IMs). Concurrently, the quantum toroidal algebra $U_q(D_l^{"})$ of type $D_l$ admits four distinct representations via free field realizations, each corresponding to one of the four end nodes of the affine Dynkin diagram. Utilizing these representations, we associate an infinite set of commuting operators with each node, which we define as non-local integrals of motion. Both local and non-local integrals of motion act simultaneously on a shared Fock space consisting of $l+1$ free fields. We provide a direct, computational proof demonstrating that these local and non-local integrals of motion mutually commute.

item.title: All-genus mirror symmetry for the type-$D$ minimal resolution Calabi-Yau threefold
item.author: Bohan Fang, Zhuoming Lan
item.description:
Bohan Fang, Zhuoming Lan

Matched: Gromov-Witten · math.AG, math-ph, math.MP · cross

Let $Y$ be the product of a minimal resolution of a binary dihedral surface singularity with an equivariant line, with volume-preserving scalar action. We identify its stable equivariant descendant Gromov--Witten theory and its free energies in genus at least two with the sign-sector topological recursion of the degenerate type-$D$ relativistic Toda spectral curve. The $R-$matrix calibration is determined at a partial large-radius limit, where the trivalent exceptional curve retains a nonzero K\"ahler parameter, while the remaining parameters vanish. The limiting theory on the mirror side is a sum of twisted point theories and the local $(-2,0)$ curve theory. Moreover, we identify the equivariant K-group supported on the surface zero section with an integral relative homology group of the mirror. Explicit cycles for the dual tautological bundles realize their Gamma central charges and all stable Gamma-framed descendants.

item.author: Renzo Cavalieri, David Klompenhouwer, Paolo Rossi
item.description:
Renzo Cavalieri, David Klompenhouwer, Paolo Rossi

Matched: KdV · math.AG, math-ph, math.MP · cross

We encode these invariants in appropriate generating functions, which we relate to the Hamiltonians of the KdV hierarchy.

item.title: Generalized Schwarzian thermodynamics from gravitational perturbations of near-extremal Kerr
item.author: Marcela C\'ardenas, Benjam\'in Cuevas-Tapia, Jessica Trespalacios
item.description:
Marcela C\'ardenas, Benjam\'in Cuevas-Tapia, Jessica Trespalacios

Matched: KdV · gr-qc, hep-th · cross

We derive the generalized Schwarzian thermodynamics of near-extremal Kerr directly from four-dimensional gravitational perturbations of the near-horizon geometry. We construct two families of exact linear perturbations of the near-NHEK background: a non-normalizable mode that deforms the asymptotic boundary, and a normalizable mode supported near the horizon. Both perturbations are smooth solutions of the vacuum Einstein equations reduced to the Jackiw--Teitelboim equation for the dual scalar, without conical singularities. We study their asymptotic symmetries and show that they generate an algebra of time reparametrizations; requiring the gauge parameters to depend on the Schwarzian mode, the isometry condition selects the stationary KdV hierarchy. The same hierarchy is independently enforced by the vacuum Einstein equations on the perturbation coefficient. In the Euclidean regime, we evaluate the Hamiltonian action and show that each mode independently generates a tower of odd-power corrections to the near-extremal entropy.

item.title: A scalable computational framework for PDEs on physical networks
item.author: Sidney Holden, Keaton J. Burns, Daniel Lecoanet, Jeffrey S. Oishi, Benjamin P. Brown, Geoffrey M. Vasil
item.description:
Sidney Holden, Keaton J. Burns, Daniel Lecoanet, Jeffrey S. Oishi, Benjamin P. Brown, Geoffrey M. Vasil

Matched: KdV · math-ph, math.MP · new

Transport, reaction and wave propagation on physical networks depend on dynamics along edges and interactions at junctions. We present a flexible framework for modeling physical networks at scale. A network calculus expresses edge dynamics and vertex contributions as fields over the whole network. Differential operators satisfy integration by parts-identities that connect local dynamics to global conservation laws, and explicit vertex constraints allow a variety of physical junction conditions. We implement this formalism using the open-source Dedalus spectral framework. This accommodates heterogeneous edge lengths, material properties and spectral resolutions. Initial-value, boundary-value and eigenvalue problems share a parallel solution method that eliminates internal unknowns independently on subgraphs and couples their solutions through shared boundary vertex interfaces. We verify numerical convergence and demonstrate strong and weak scaling on networks with millions of edges. We present applications to localized optical resonances in photonic networks, preferential channel formation during mineral replacement in evolving pore networks, and nonlinear dispersive waves for KdV on a periodic network.

item.title: On Fujita's Advanced Generalized Mukai Conjecture
item.author: Duo Li
item.description:
Duo Li

Matched: Gromov-Witten · math.AG · new

We prove Fujita's advanced generalized Mukai conjecture for smooth complex Fano varieties. Our starting point is the existence of independent two-point Gromov--Witten correspondences. We show that there are finitely many unsplit families of rational curves whose chains connect $X$. We use these families to bound the anticanonical degrees throughout the successive minimal horizontal construction, so every family in that construction is unsplit. Fujita's contraction theorem and inductive classification then give the required list of varieties.

item.title: Toward Shifted symplectic Chiralization: Deformation of Courant Algebroids
item.author: Wenda Fang, Noriaki Ikeda
item.description:
Wenda Fang, Noriaki Ikeda

Matched: integrable hierarch · math.QA, math-ph, math.MP, math.SG · cross

We study the chiralization of Poisson--Lie theory through graded symplectic geometry. We compare Courant deformations and classical $r$- and $R$-matrix constructions, obtaining integrable hierarchies and free field realizations. We give a variational description of the obstruction to Lie conformal bialgebra compatibility and recover Liberati's obstruction in the Virasoro case. We also introduce a vertex bialgebra analogue of quantized universal enveloping algebras and construct explicit quantizations to all orders of Cartan type Lie conformal bialgebra structures on $\operatorname{Cur}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$. These results contribute to the first author's broader programme of developing shifted symplectic chiralization as a geometric method for constructing chiral analogues of Poisson-Lie structures via $n$-shifted symplectic geometry, and exploring its connections with AKSZ theory and quantization.

item.title: Concavity of Normalized Generalized Br\'ezin--Gross--Witten Correlators and Its Applications
item.author: Chenglang Yang, Xuhui Zhang
item.description:
Chenglang Yang, Xuhui Zhang

Matched: tau function · math-ph, math.AG, math.MP · new

In this paper, we study the generalized Br\'ezin--Gross--Witten model using its BKP integrability. By virtue of the formula for connected $n$-point functions of tau-functions of the BKP hierarchy obtained by Wang and the first-named author, we prove that the normalized generalized BGW correlators are strictly concave for fixed genus and fixed total degree. As applications, we establish the strict Schur-concavity and derive upper and lower bounds for these correlators. We also prove the strict monotonicity of normalized ordinary BGW correlators, which resolves a conjecture by Guo--Norbury--Yang--Zagier.

item.title: An Explicit Construction of Commuting Quantum KdV Hamiltonians in the Universal Virasoro Vertex Algebra
item.author: Hongbo Zhao
item.description:
Hongbo Zhao

Matched: KdV · math.QA · new

We give an explicit formula for elements $H_{2k}$ of conformal weight $2k$, $k\ge1$, in the universal Virasoro vertex operator algebra $V$ at every central charge, such that $H_{2k}(0)H_{2l}\in TV$ for all $k,l\ge1$. Modulo translation, the kernel of $H_4(0)$ is generated by $[H_{2k}]$ in each positive even weight and is zero in positive odd weights. The formula uses a realization on differential polynomials by possibly infinite-order differential operators in a completion of the Weyl algebra, together with the inverse of the identity plus a nilpotent operator on each weight space. A Koszul-type exactness argument for the classical KdV flows proves conservation; uniqueness and the Jacobi identity give commutativity. The classical limit recovers the normalized Gelfand--Dickey densities. Explicit low-weight elements and exact symbolic verifications illustrate the construction.

item.title: Pure Spinor Factorization of Belinski-Zakharov Solitons and Regular Gravitational Instantons
item.author: Steffen Aksteiner
item.description:
Steffen Aksteiner

Matched: tau function · math.DG, gr-qc · new

We show that the Belinski-Zakharov soliton construction factorizes into signed Pfaffian tau-functions, revealing a pure-spinor description of the metric and its regularity conditions. We derive analytic restrictions on the integral rod data, prove uniqueness for the asymptotically flat balance problem at fixed rod structure and periods, and give a conditional criterion for global existence. Combining these results with exhaustive enumeration of the admissible data and rigorous existence certificates, we construct a catalogue of regular asymptotically flat solutions representing 356 rod-word classes through twelve turning points, and 52 isolated regular asymptotically locally flat solutions through eight turning points. Analytic positivity and smooth-completion results establish regularity beyond the finite numerical solve. Based on this catalogue, we investigate two organizations of the solution space: generalized rank-two root systems and compositions of simpler endpoint geometries. The endpoint composition rules reproduce exactly all retained asymptotically flat words through twelve turning points.

item.title: Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz for the Toda chain from inverse scattering transform
item.author: Alberto Brollo
item.description:
Alberto Brollo

Matched: KdV · cond-mat.stat-mech, math-ph, math.MP, nlin.SI · cross

The Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz (TBA) procedure developed by Yang-Yang provides the free energy functional to be minimized via a variational problem. Their result not only gives the correct thermodynamics, but it also sets the framework for Generalized Hydrodynamics. Originally developed for quantum systems, this procedure has been recently successfully applied to (integrable) classical particle systems. However, this has never been done for classical field theories: no classical derivation has consistently accounted for solitons, breathers, radiation (dispersive modes), and their mutual interactions. We here derive the TBA equations for the Toda chain directly from its inverse scattering transform. This results in solitonic modes interacting with radiation, extending the soliton gas picture. We provide numerical verification of our equations against well established TBA equations in terms of particle modes. We expect the same procedure should apply to KdV, and pure radiative models as defocusing NLS and Sinh-Gordon, while we discuss current limitations in other models such as focusing NLS (and Ablowitz-Ladik) and Sine-Gordon.

item.title: Modular properties of correlators in generalised Gibbs ensembles
item.author: Tanmoy Sengupta
item.description:
Tanmoy Sengupta

Matched: KdV · hep-th · new

We study the modular properties of torus correlators in a generalised Gibbs ensemble (GGE) of a two-dimensional conformal field theory. For the free fermion with KdV charges, we compute the exact two-point function and derive its modular $S$-transformation as a formal power series in the chemical potential. The transformed correlator admits a factorised description: an effective charge deforms the ensemble, while a local dressing operator acts on the external fields. Both are determined by nested operator product expansions involving the deforming current. Motivated by this result, we conjecture an analogous transformation law for $n$-point functions in rational chiral conformal field theories. Using Zhu's recursion, we establish the conjecture at the lowest explicit power of the modular parameter to all orders in the chemical potential, thereby determining the dressing operator. We also verify the full conjectured transformation through cubic order in the chemical potential, retaining all explicit powers of the modular parameter. These results extend the nested-OPE description of modular transformations of GGE partition functions to local correlation functions.

item.author: Dang Tuan Hiep, Ha Thi Thao Tram
item.description:
Dang Tuan Hiep, Ha Thi Thao Tram

Matched: Gromov-Witten · math.AG · new

We compare genus zero degree two Gromov--Witten invariants with the number of embedded conics on general projective complete intersections whose conic space has expected dimension zero. Their difference comes from double covers of lines. We compute this contribution as an integral of Chern classes over the Fano scheme of lines, using an explicit obstruction bundle on the compactified space of double covers.

item.title: Multiplicity and parity in Hirota's $N$-soliton conditions: the bilinear families $L\,(D_x^{3}+\Lambda)^{2n+1}$
item.author: Shi Zhenhua
item.description:
Shi Zhenhua

Matched: Korteweg-de Vries · math-ph, math.MP · new

Hirota's three-soliton condition is the standard test for the integrability of a bilinear equation $P(D)f\cdot f=0$, and the folklore implication ``three-soliton condition $\Rightarrow$ $N$-soliton solutions for all $N$'' underlies the classifications of Hietarinta. We study this implication in two directions. The first is the family $L\,(D_x^3+\Lambda)^{2n+1}f\cdot f=0$ with $L$, $\Lambda$ linear forms in the Hirota operators, which for $n=0$ contains the Korteweg--de Vries, Ito and Boiti--Leon--Manna--Pempinelli equations and for $L=D_x$ is the family of G\"urses and Pekcan. On the principal component of the dispersion variety the $N$-soliton condition reduces to a sign sum of two bialternants; counting odd exponents shows that for $n=0$ the class is Hirota integrable and that for $n\ge1$ the three-soliton condition holds for every $L$, and an explicit formula for the four-soliton residual proves the G\"urses--Pekcan conjecture that the four-soliton condition fails for every $n\ge1$. The formula yields sum-of-squares certificates excluding four-soliton solutions at every real configuration for the G\"urses--Pekcan and Ito equations, classifies the real members of the class, and determines maximal numbers of nondegenerate solitons: exactly four or five for $n=1$ according as $L$ lies in the span of $D_x,\Lambda$ or not, five for $n=2$ and $L=D_x$, and finite for every $n\ge1$ and every $L$. The second direction is a reformulation of the implication for a single non-hyperplane component of multiplicity one, which we prove, with complete classifications, for all graph-type dispersions $L(q(D)+D_t)$, for every irreducible even quadric component in any dimension and with an arbitrary cofactor, for parabolic components, for the dispersions $F(\ell)+Q$ containing the Kadomtsev--Petviashvili surface, and, with a prescribed one-parameter phase family, for the cubic graph.

item.title: Mapping-space Gromov--Witten classes and the Fano variety of lines
item.author: Ivan Smith, Abigail Ward
item.description:
Ivan Smith, Abigail Ward

Matched: Gromov-Witten · math.SG · new

Let $Y$ be a smooth cubic 3-fold. We show that $S^2 \times Y$ admits an infinite sequence of cohomologous symplectic forms which are all deformation equivalent but pairwise non-isotopic; McDuff showed the corresponding result on $(S^2)^2 \times T^2$, but these appear to be the first simply-connected and monotone examples. The results are obtained from McDuff's bordism-flavoured Gromov--Witten invariant, re-interpreted cohomologically in terms of an evaluation map valued in the space of maps from the 2-sphere to a symplectic target. The application then relies on classical properties of the Fano space of lines on $Y$. We also discuss higher-dimensional generalisations.

item.title: Gromov-Witten theory of the local model of the standard flop
item.author: Alex D\"anzer, Yannik Schuler
item.description:
Alex D\"anzer, Yannik Schuler

Matched: Gromov-Witten · math.AG · new

We conjecture that the generating series of equivariant Gromov-Witten invariants of the local Calabi-Yau $(2n-1)$-fold $\operatorname{Tot} \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^{n-1}} (-1)^{\oplus n}$ at fixed genus can be presented as a linear combination of polylogarithms, generalising a well-known property of the resolved conifold. We prove this conjecture for two specialisations of the equivariant parameters. In the first, the parameters are specialised to roots of unity and the proof proceeds via Givental-Teleman reconstruction. In the second, we obtain a closed-form evaluation of the generating series from which the conjecture follows. For $n=3$, the resulting closed formula establishes a special case of a Gopakumar-Vafa-type conjecture for Calabi-Yau fivefolds.

item.title: Universal Curve Counting in Calabi-Yau 4-folds
item.author: Ivan Karpov, Felix Thimm
item.description:
Ivan Karpov, Felix Thimm

Matched: Gromov-Witten · math.AG, hep-th, math.SG · cross

Recently, Pardon introduced a universal curve counting framework, which allows him to show that curve counting on 3-folds is "generated" by local curves (in a precise sense). We implement this universal curve counting program for Calabi-Yau 4-folds, where a significant technical difficulty comes from the dependence of the virtual dimension on the genus, which leads to more complicated generators than just local curves. Our main techniques are combinations of deformation-theoretic and homotopy-theoretic methods with an adaptation of Pardon's generic transversality results, which allow us to establish a full set of (computable) generators for CY4 curve counting. As a result, we prove (a slight correction of) the Gromov-Witten/Pandharipande-Thomas correspondence with primary descendents for CY4-folds, formulated by Cao, Maulik, and Toda. From this, we additionally obtain integrality of Gopakumar-Vafa style invariants for CY4-folds, as conjectured by Klemm-Pandharipande.

item.title: Correlators of the Jacobi Unitary Ensemble on a General Interval and Hurwitz Numbers
item.author: Matvey Sushkov
item.description:
Matvey Sushkov

Matched: tau function · math-ph, math.CO, math.MP, math.PR, math.RT, nlin.SI · cross

We study correlators of the Jacobi Unitary Ensemble $\mathbf J(p,q,\alpha,\beta,N)$ of Hermitian matrices with spectrum in an arbitrary real interval $[p,q]$. For $(p,q)=(0,1)$, Gisonni, Grava and Ruzza expressed the large-$N$ expansion of the correlators $\langle\prod_j \mathrm{tr}\,X^{\lambda_j}\rangle$ through triple monotone Hurwitz numbers. We extend this genus expansion to arbitrary $p,q$ with $\alpha/N$ and $\beta/N$ fixed. Using the Frobenius characteristic map and the idempotent basis of the center of $\mathbb C[\mathfrak S_n]$, we also obtain an explicit formula for the Schur--Selberg type integral $\int_{(p,q)^N}\chi_\lambda(x)\,\Delta^2(x)\prod_a (q-x_a)^\beta (x_a-p)^\alpha\,\mathrm{d}^Nx$ in terms of irreducible characters of the symmetric group and content products. As consequences, we describe the zero-mean ensemble, and we recover, term by term in the genus expansion, the polygon-gluing formula for the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble in the limit $c_A=c_B\to\infty$. Structurally, passing from $[0,1]$ to $[p,q]$ leaves the hypergeometric weight of the associated 2D Toda tau function unchanged and only changes the specialization of its second set of times.

item.title: Elliptic soliton solutions of lattice eigenfunction equations of the KdV type
item.author: Xing Li, Ying Shi, Da-jun Zhang, Ruixiao Zhu
item.description:
Xing Li, Ying Shi, Da-jun Zhang, Ruixiao Zhu

Matched: KdV, Korteweg-de Vries · nlin.SI · new

It is known that some integrable lattice equations can be formulated by the eigenfunctions of the Lax triplet of the lattice potential Korteweg-de Vries (lpKdV) equation; the eigenfunctions satisfy a discrete Abel formula in which the `integration' constant defines the $\delta$ parameter in some equations in the Adler-Bobenko-Suris (ABS) classification. In this paper, we present a full Darboux transformation for the Lax triplet of the lpKdV equation, and eigenfunctions are formulated in terms of Casoratians. When the eigenfunctions take the elementary discrete Lam\'e functions, we get the elliptic $N$-soliton solution for the lpKdV equation after $N$-fold Darboux transformation. We then determine the constant in the discrete Abel formula in this case. The eigenfunctions are used to formulate elliptic $N$-soliton solutions for various equations in the ABS list, such as H3($\delta$), $Q1(\Delta)$, Q2 and Q3($\Delta$) equations.

item.title: Resurgence and Modularity in the First Painlev\'e Equation
item.author: Kohei Iwaki, Noam Tamarin
item.description:
Kohei Iwaki, Noam Tamarin

Matched: tau function · hep-th, math-ph, math.MP · new

For the first Painlev\'e equation, we relate three nonlinear Stokes maps associated with a full turn around infinity to modular transformations of the two-parameter tau function through the identity $\boldsymbol S_\pi\circ\boldsymbol S_0\circ \boldsymbol S_{-\pi}=\mathsf S\circ\mathsf T$. Working under the analytic assumptions of the topological recursion and exact WKB constructions, we compare Stokes multipliers of the associated isomonodromy system while tracking the homology basis of its elliptic spectral curve under rotations of the independent variable. For the sectors considered, we identify the known parameter transformation induced by an $8\pi/5$ rotation with the modular $T$-action and derive a new explicit parameter relation realizing the $S$-action for a $2\pi/5$ rotation. We also determine the multiplicative factors in the corresponding tau-function relations, including their normalization constants. Together, these results give an explicit realization of single-valuedness after one full turn around infinity for both the Painlev\'e transcendent and its tau function, with the tau-function prefactors cancelling by Abel's five-term identity for the Rogers dilogarithm.

item.author: Jianjun Fu, Shuai Guo, Qingsheng Zhang
item.description:
Jianjun Fu, Shuai Guo, Qingsheng Zhang

item.title: Effective Gromov-Witten computations for GKM spaces and a semisimple application
item.author: Daniel Holmes, Giosu\`e Muratore
item.description:
Daniel Holmes, Giosu\`e Muratore

Matched: Gromov-Witten · math.AG, math.SG · cross

These are precisely the remaining exceptional Grassmannians for which generic semisimplicity of small quantum cohomology was still unknown.

item.title: Uniform asymptotics and the Weil--Petersson constant
item.author: Kefeng Liu, Hao Xu
item.description:
Kefeng Liu, Hao Xu

Matched: KdV · math.AG · new

In their celebrated work on the large-genus asymptotic expansion of Weil--Petersson volumes, Mirzakhani and Zograf left open the question of whether the Weil--Petersson constant satisfies $C_{\mathrm{WP}}=\pi^{-1/2}$. We resolve the conjecture affirmatively. Our strategy is to consider a family of spectral curves interpolating between $y=z-4z^3$ and $y=\sin(2\pi z)/(2\pi)$. For each fixed number $n\geq2$ of marked points, we normalize the cusp coefficients using the action integral and the derivative at its first positive zero. We prove that the logarithmic derivatives of these normalized coefficients with respect to the family parameter are $O_n(g^{-1})$, uniformly along the family. The proof combines the descendant recursion, positivity, the dilaton equation, KdV, and coefficient asymptotics for the Painlev\'e I equation.

item.title: Universal polynomials for Gromov-Witten invariants on toric surfaces
item.author: Yanqiao Ding, Dadi Ni
item.description:
Yanqiao Ding, Dadi Ni

Matched: Gromov-Witten · math.AG · new

We study the polynomiality of combined logarithmic and ordinary Gromov-Witten invariants with a Lambda class insertion on toric surfaces $\Delta(\mathbf{c},\mathbf{d})$. We show that the combined logarithmic Gromov-Witten invariants can be expressed in terms of universal relative node polynomials when the direction vector $\mathbf{c}$ and length vector $\mathbf{d}$ of the $h$-transverse lattice polygon $\Delta(\mathbf{c},\mathbf{d})$ are sufficiently large and spread out.
